newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends lower, further losses seen.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends lower, further losses seen.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed weaker and near the lows amid steady speculative liquidation in front-month July, traders said.
July fell to a nine-day low of 11.22 cents in early dealings, before the trade emerged to block additional losses and carry the contract to the day's high of 11.37 cents.
Trade selling pushed the market back towards the middle of the range where it drifted until a late bout of speculative selling took prices back towards the day's lows.

Market sources expect prices to work lower ahead of the July expiry on June 30. The speculators maintain a heavy net long position in July, dealers said, citing open of 75,212 lots in July, as of early Tuesday.
Friday's options expiry should speed liquidation, dealers said.

The July contract closed 0.11 cent lower at 11.26 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.37 to 11.22 cents. October eased 0.10 cent on the day to close at 11.15 cents, while the outer months ended 0.06 and 0.05 cent weaker.
Early speculative selling pressured benchmark July to its low of 11.22 cents, where the trade prevented the contract from sinking to support at 11.20 cents.
Trade selling at the day's high of 11.37 cents limited gains as volume thinned by the close.
Analysts said the July contract could retreat to 11.00 cents over the next week, and cited sell stops around 11.12 cents.
An estimated 24,817 lots changed hands on the day compared with Tuesday's official 24,622 lots.
